fixes.old: 0: no evidence. 1: mostly general evidence, little commentary. 2: some specific evidence, but summary rather than explanation. 3: specific evidence for most claims, with commentary that mostly explains how it supports the argument. 4: consistent specific evidence plus commentary that explains the reasoning throughout.
fixes.new: 0: no relevant evidence, or the response only restates the thesis. 1: mostly general evidence, and/or evidence summarized rather than explained. 2: some specific relevant evidence, with explanation of how some of it relates to the argument, but no line of reasoning is established or the line of reasoning is faulty. 3: specific evidence to support all claims in a line of reasoning, with explanation of how some of the evidence supports that line of reasoning. 4: specific evidence for all claims in a line of reasoning, with commentary that consistently explains how the evidence supports it.
fixes.why: Misstates the official Row B scale: 'specific evidence but summary rather than explanation' is a 1, not a 2, and a 3 requires evidence for all claims in a line of reasoning, not most.

fixes.old: The jump from 2 to 3 is the jump from summarizing evidence to explaining it.
fixes.new: The jump from 1 to 2 is the jump from summarizing evidence to explaining it; the jump from 2 to 3 is establishing a real line of reasoning.
fixes.why: The summary-to-explanation jump happens at 1 to 2 on the AP rubric; 2 to 3 is where a line of reasoning appears.

fixes.old: The thesis may appear anywhere, but placing it last in paragraph one is the safest way to secure Row A.
fixes.new: The thesis must appear in the introduction or the conclusion; placing it last in paragraph one is the safest way to secure Row A.
fixes.why: Contradicts the AP rubric (and card f4b7b18460): a thesis placed anywhere other than the intro or conclusion earns no Row A point.

fixes.old: On Q2, textual evidence without commentary earns at most 2 of 4 in Row B.
fixes.new: On Q2, textual evidence without commentary earns at most 1 of 4 in Row B.
fixes.why: Row B 2 requires explaining how some evidence relates to the argument, so evidence with no commentary caps at 1, not 2.

fixes.old: Roughly 60% reading-analysis and 40% writing/revision questions - budget about 80 seconds per question.
fixes.new: Roughly 23-25 reading-analysis questions and 20-22 writing/revision questions - budget about 80 seconds per question.
fixes.why: The CED splits the 45 MC questions 23-25 reading / 20-22 writing (about 55/45), not 60/40.

fixes.old: Each essay is scored holistically against the 6-point analytic rubric by a trained reader, independently of your other essays, and readers are instructed to reward what the response does well rather than deduct for what is missing.
fixes.new: Each essay is scored row by row against the 6-point analytic rubric by a trained reader, independently of your other essays, and readers are instructed to reward what the response does well rather than deduct for what is missing.
fixes.why: AP Lang essays have been scored with analytic row-by-row rubrics since 2019, not holistically; 'scored holistically against the analytic rubric' is self-contradictory and misleading.

fixes.old: A syllogism can be valid but untrue: valid form plus false premise still yields a false conclusion.
fixes.new: A syllogism can be valid but unsound: valid form plus a false premise guarantees nothing about whether the conclusion is true.
fixes.why: A valid argument with a false premise can still have a true conclusion, so 'still yields a false conclusion' is logically wrong.

fixes.old: Identify six qualifiers a writer can use to limit a claim.
fixes.new: Identify eight qualifiers a writer can use to limit a claim.
fixes.why: The question asks for six qualifiers but the answer lists eight, so the card can never be self-checked correctly.

fixes.old: A composite in the low-to-mid 60s percent range typically reaches a 3; exact cut scores shift each year.
fixes.new: A composite around half the available points typically reaches a 3; exact cut scores shift each year.
fixes.why: A low-to-mid 60s percent composite is historically in 4 territory on AP Lang; the 3 cut sits near 50-55 percent.
